title: Input to the `review.search` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `review.search`. SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2).

**Unknown keys are refused rather than dropped.** The SDK sets no `extra="forbid"` on the argument model it derives from the handler, so a key it does not recognise is discarded before any Theurian code runs, and a filtered question answered without one of its filters reads as the whole answer (ADR-0031 decision 4).

**Composition.** The context — `projectId`, and the optional `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` — arrives by `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json`. The closure is `unevaluatedProperties: false` and not `additionalProperties: false`, which under a `$ref` composition rejects the very context fields it referenced (ADR-0031 decision 1, measured against `jsonschema` 4.26.0). `projectId` is required by the referent and is not repeated here. `snapshotId`, `agentId` and `taskId` are accepted and read by no handler in this build.

**`threadState`'s vocabulary is deliberately not published here as an `enum`**, for the reason its sibling `review.findings` records for `reviewer` and `severity`: the handler's refusal names every token, recomputed from the enum rather than transcribed, and ends with a remedy an `enum` keyword cannot carry. The vocabulary is published in `review-search-response.schema.json`, where a client reads it without a refusal having to be worsened to say it.

What this file holds is shape and length. Every filter here is matched against a stored column and reaches no filesystem call — `filePath` included, which is a path as data and never a path to open (SEC-7, ADR-0030 decision 6).

repository.description:
Which repository's review records to search, as the ingested record spells it.

At most 400 characters, the bound every `review.search` filter shares. It is an amplification bound rather than a description of the data: it exists so a refusal cannot quote an arbitrary-length value back at the caller who sent it (#17). An empty string is refused by the handler, because it matches nothing rather than everything.

pullRequest.description:
Which pull request's review records to search.

No published `minimum` or `maximum`, although the column behind it is a signed 64-bit integer and the handler refuses anything outside it: binding a wider value raises an `OverflowError` no layer converts, so the bound is checked at the boundary where it can be a refusal a caller acts on. A range here would leave that guard reachable by no request.

threadState.description:
Which thread state to search — a closed vocabulary the handler names in full when it refuses, recomputed from the enum rather than transcribed. Bounded at 400 characters for the reason `repository` records.

A record that is not a thread at all is matched by omitting this filter, never by a token meaning "any": absence and a wildcard would be two spellings of one question, and one of them would drift.

author.description: Which author's review records to search. Author-controlled text on both sides of the comparison, bounded here and carried as data; the response's own schema records how the served value is labelled and cut.

filePath.description:
Which file's review records to search, as the record spells the path.

**A path as data, never a path to open.** It is matched against a stored column and reaches no filesystem call, here or below (SEC-7, ADR-0030 decision 6), so nothing in it is resolved, contained or followed. Bounded at 400 characters for the reason `repository` records.

q.description: Free text to match against the stored review evidence. Bounded at 400 characters for the reason `repository` records; an empty string is refused by the handler, because it matches nothing rather than everything.

limit.description:
How many records to return. Defaults to 20, and the ceiling is a **refusal** rather than a clamp: this tool answers a filtered question with no paging, so a silently truncated page reads as the whole answer to the filter (`theurian.mcp.review_search.MAX_REVIEW_SEARCH_LIMIT`).

No published `minimum` or `maximum`: the handler's refusal names both ends and says why it is not a clamp, and a range here would answer "does not satisfy" in its place.
